object_server and object_client

The database object server example tools: store and read objects, and ask for vector searches (Linux and Windows).

Contents

Usage

Usage

object_server PORT CERT KEY CA CLIENT_CN DB_NAME DB_FILE [--stop-file FILE]
object_client HOST PORT SERVER_NAME CERT KEY CA DB_NAME "text"
object_client HOST PORT SERVER_NAME CERT KEY CA DB_NAME --vinfo
object_client HOST PORT SERVER_NAME CERT KEY CA DB_NAME --vsearch K   < query (whitespace separated floats)

object_server serves one database with mutual TLS (only CLIENT_CN may connect). object_client stores a text object and reads it back, or with --vinfo / --vsearch asks a server whose database names its vectors (a gxObjectDbConfig with vectors) for the index's description or the K nearest to the query on stdin. The requests: Object Server Vector Searches; a complete program: vector_search_service.

Stopping the server: Ctrl+C, or TERM on Linux; Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Break or closing the console on Windows; or, on both, creating the file given with --stop-file (checked every second; a service wrapper or a script uses this). Clients get up to 10 seconds to finish. Windows (7.4): the same programs over Winsock and Schannel, and they work with Linux servers and clients both ways. The multiplex never blocks on a TLS write, so two sides that both send large messages at once do not wait on each other (gxdbmux_test both_ways_large_tls checks this on both systems).
